mainTopic: The mission to Rome, and when different foods and kinds of טומאה join to reach a minimum amount
overview: The amud finishes the story of the mission to Rome. רבי שמעון בן יוחאי is chosen because he is used to miracles, and רבי אלעזר בר רבי יוסי goes with him. On the way, רבי אלעזר answers a halachic question in front of his teacher, and רבי שמעון punishes him. A demon, בן תמליון, offers help and enters the emperor's daughter. רבי שמעון drives it out, and the grateful emperor lets the רבנן into his treasury, where they tear up the decree. The amud then turns to halacha with a new משנה: פיגול and נותר, and different sources of טומאה, do not join to reach a minimum amount. שמואל limits the rule about פיגול and נותר to טומאת ידים, because for eating one shared איסור covers both. A second משנה teaches that food at different levels of טומאה, and all foods or all liquids, do join for many standard amounts. רבא and רב אשי each explain why a ראשון and a שני join together.

steps.title: The Sages pick who will go to Rome
steps.stepSummary: The חכמים decide that רבי שמעון בן יוחאי should go, because he is used to miracles, and that רבי אלעזר בר רבי יוסי should go with him.
steps.simpleTranslation: Let רבי שמעון בן יוחאי go, since he is used to miracles. And who will go with him? רבי אלעזר בר רבי יוסי.
steps.whatsHappening: The חכמים choose the people for the dangerous mission to Rome. They pick רבי שמעון בן יוחאי and give him רבי אלעזר בר רבי יוסי as a companion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The trip is dangerous, so they choose someone who can rely on miracles to protect him. A second person, רבי אלעזר בר רבי יוסי, is named to go along. This choice is what sets off the argument that follows.

keyTerms.meaning: Used to miracles; someone for whom miracles often happen
And after him, meaning together with him as a companion

phrases.english: Let Rabbi Shimon ben Yoḥai go,
as he is used to miracles.
And who will go after him?
phrases.notes: "After him" here means alongside him, as his travel partner.

phrases.english: Rabbi Elazar bar Rabbi Yosei.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the story from earlier on the daf, where the חכמים are deciding who should go to Rome.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי שמעון בן יוחאי will go, and רבי אלעזר בר רבי יוסי will go with him.

steps.title: רבי יוסי objects to sending his son
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי protests: if my father אבא חלפתא were alive, could you ask him to hand over his son to be killed?
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוסי said to them: If אבא חלפתא were alive, could you say to him, 'Give your son to be killed'?
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוסי, the father of רבי אלעזר, objects to the plan. He argues that you cannot ask a father to send his son into deadly danger.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He makes his point through his own father: no one would have dared ask אבא חלפתא to give up his son, who is רבי יוסי himself. By the same reasoning, they should not ask רבי יוסי to give up his son. The objection is aimed at sending רבי אלעזר.

keyTerms.meaning: If, in a case that is not actually true

phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei said to them:
But if Abba Ḥalafta were alive,
phrases.notes: אבא חלפתא is רבי יוסי's own father, so the "son" in this question is רבי יוסי himself.

phrases.english: would you be able to say to him:
Give your son to be killed?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Objects to the second half of step 1, the choice of רבי אלעזר as companion.
steps.kashyaTarget: The decision to send רבי אלעזר בר רבי יוסי to Rome
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A father cannot be asked to hand over his son to likely death. He shows this from his own father, אבא חלפתא.

steps.title: רבי שמעון answers: I am risking my life too
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון answers with the same words: if my father יוחאי were alive, could you ask him to give his son to be killed? I am going anyway.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמעון said to them: If my father יוחאי were alive, could you say to him, 'Give your son to be killed'?
steps.whatsHappening: רבי שמעון answers רבי יוסי's protest by turning the same argument around. He is also someone's son, and he is still willing to go.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He repeats רבי יוסי's exact words but puts his own father in place of אבא חלפתא. The point is that everyone on this trip is risking his life. Since רבי שמעון accepts that danger, the danger alone is not a reason to keep רבי אלעזר home.

phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon said to them:
If Yoḥai, my father, were alive,
would you be able to say to him:
Give your son to be killed?
phrases.notes: He doesn't say it outright, but he means: I'm going anyway, so רבי אלעזר can come too.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבי יוסי's objection in step 2 using the same wording.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Turning the same argument back on the objector
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The danger to a son is a reason not to send רבי אלעזר.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי שמעון faces the same danger and is still going, so the danger does not cancel the plan.

steps.title: רבי יוסי reveals his real fear
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי offers to go himself, because he is afraid that רבי שמעון will punish his son.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוסי said to them: I will go, because I am afraid that רבי שמעון might punish him.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוסי changes his argument. He now says what really worries him: that רבי שמעון, who is quick to anger, will punish his young son on the way.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The problem is no longer the danger of Rome. It is the danger of traveling with רבי שמעון. So רבי יוסי offers to go in his son's place. This prepares the promise and its outcome in the next step.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לְהוּ רַבִּי יוֹסֵי: אֲנָא אָזְלִין,
phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei said to them: I will go,
lest Rabbi Shimon punish him,
phrases.notes: "Him" is רבי יוסי's son, רבי אלעזר.

phrases.english: for this is what I fear.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לְהוּ רַבִּי יוֹסֵי: אֲנָא אָזְלִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After רבי שמעון's answer, רבי יוסי moves from the danger of Rome to his fear of רבי שמעון himself.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי יוסי offers to go in place of his son, out of fear that רבי שמעון will punish him.

steps.title: רבי שמעון promises, but punishes him anyway
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון promises not to punish רבי אלעזר, but in the end he does punish him.
steps.simpleTranslation: He took it upon himself not to punish him. Even so, he punished him.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי שמעון promises not to punish רבי אלעזר, so the son goes. The גמרא then tells us in advance that the punishment happened anyway, and the next step explains how.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The promise answers רבי יוסי's fear, so the plan goes ahead with רבי אלעזר. The words "even so, he punished him" set up the story on the road. The reader now waits to learn what led to it.

phrases.english: He took it upon himself that he would not punish him.
phrases.notes: רבי שמעון is the one promising, and the one he promises not to punish is רבי אלעזר.

phrases.english: Even so, he punished him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבי יוסי's fear from step 4 with a promise, then tells us the promise was not kept.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי שמעון promised not to punish רבי אלעזר, yet he punished him.

steps.title: On the road: the question about the blood of a שרץ
steps.stepSummary: While traveling, they are asked where we learn that the blood of a שרץ is טמא. רבי אלעזר twists his mouth and quietly answers with a פסוק.
steps.simpleTranslation: While they were walking on the road, this question was asked in front of them: From where do we know that the blood of a שרץ is טמא? רבי אלעזר בר רבי יוסי twisted his mouth and said: 'And this is the impure for you.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now explains what led to the punishment. A halachic question comes up on the road, and רבי אלעזר answers it quietly, twisting his mouth so רבי שמעון will not notice.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question asks for a source showing that a שרץ's blood carries טומאה. רבי אלעזר answers with a פסוק about טמא creeping creatures. He twists his mouth to hide that he is speaking, which shows he knew answering in front of his teacher was a problem.

keyTerms.meaning: The blood of a creeping creature
He twisted his mouth, to speak quietly

phrases.english: When they were walking on the road,
this question was asked before them:
From where do we know that the blood of a creeping creature is impure?

phrases.aramaic: עִקֵּם פִּיו רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בַּר רַבִּי יוֹסֵי,
phrases.english: Rabbi Elazar bar Rabbi Yosei twisted his mouth,
phrases.notes: He was trying to whisper so his teacher wouldn't hear him.

phrases.english: and said: “And this is the impure for you.”
phrases.notes: ויקרא 11:29

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the background to the punishment mentioned in step 5.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The source showing that the blood of a שרץ is טמא
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רבי אלעזר quietly cites "וזה לכם הטמא".

steps.title: רבי שמעון praises him, then declares the punishment
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון says the twist of his lips shows he is a תלמיד חכם, yet declares that the son will not return to his father.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמעון said to him: From the twisting of your lips I can tell you are a תלמיד חכם. Let the son not return to his father.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי שמעון catches what רבי אלעזר did. He praises his learning, then pronounces the punishment: רבי אלעזר will not come home to his father.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is the punishment the גמרא told us about in advance in step 5, and the very thing רבי יוסי feared in step 4. The praise and the curse come together: the answer was good, but giving it in front of his teacher was not allowed. So רבי שמעון did end up punishing רבי יוסי's son.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not think רבי אלעזר was punished for a wrong answer. רבי שמעון actually praises him as a תלמיד חכם. The usual explanation is that a student may not give a halachic ruling in front of his teacher.
steps.whatToRemember: רבי יוסי feared that רבי שמעון would punish his son, and even after promising not to, רבי שמעון cursed him after he answered a halachic question in his teacher's presence.

phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon said to him:
From the twisting of your lips you are recognizable
that you are a Torah scholar,
let the son not return to his father.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן: מֵעֲקִימַת שְׂפָתֶיךָ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Reacts to רבי אלעזר's quiet answer in step 6 and carries out the punishment told in step 5.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: רבי שמעון recognized רבי אלעזר as a תלמיד חכם but punished him for answering in his presence, so רבי יוסי's fear came true.

steps.title: A demon offers help and רבי שמעון cries
steps.stepSummary: The demon בן תמליון offers to join the רבנן. רבי שמעון cries that הגר got an angel three times while he gets none, but he accepts the help anyway.
steps.simpleTranslation: בן תמליון came out to greet him and said: Do you want me to come with you? רבי שמעון cried and said: A maidservant of my father's house had an angel come to her three times, and I don't get one even once? Still, let the miracle come any way it can.
steps.whatsHappening: The story goes on. A demon offers to help save the Jews, and רבי שמעון is hurt that his help is a demon and not an angel, but he says yes.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי שמעון compares himself to הגר, the maid of אברהם, who met angels three times. He feels he should deserve at least as much. But saving the Jews matters more than how the help arrives, so he accepts it.

keyTerms.meaning: Maidservant (here הגר, the maid in אברהם's home)
In any case; no matter how

phrases.english: Ben Temalyon came out to greet him:
phrases.notes: בן תמליון is a demon (a שד), not a person.

phrases.english: Do you want me to come with you?
Rabbi Shimon cried and said:
What! The maidservant of my father's house
phrases.notes: He means הגר, the maid of אברהם, our forefather.

phrases.english: had an angel appear to her three times.
phrases.notes: בראשית 16:9–11

phrases.english: And I, not even one time?
Let the miracle come, no matter how.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the journey to Rome described in the earlier steps.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי שמעון accepts help from a demon, because the miracle matters more than how it comes.

steps.title: The demon is driven out and the decree is torn up
steps.stepSummary: The demon enters the emperor's daughter. רבי שמעון calls it out, the emperor thanks them with access to his treasury, and they find and tear up the letter with the decree.
steps.simpleTranslation: The demon went ahead and entered the emperor's daughter. When רבי שמעון arrived, he said: Ben Temalyon, come out! Ben Temalyon, come out! Once he was called, he came out and left. The emperor said to them: Ask for whatever you want. He brought them into his treasury to take whatever they wished. They found that letter, took it and tore it up.
steps.whatsHappening: This is the high point of the story. The plan works: the princess is healed and the רבנן destroy the decree against the Jews.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The demon creates the problem, and רבי שמעון solves it in front of the emperor. The emperor's thanks gives the רבנן the chance they need, and tearing up the letter cancels the decree. This closes the mission that started in the earlier steps.

keyTerms.meaning: Come out! (the command to the demon)

steps.whatToRemember: The miracle came through a demon, but it fully worked: the decree against the Jews was torn up.

phrases.english: He went ahead of them
and entered into the emperor's daughter.
When he arrived there, he said:
phrases.notes: "He" here is רבי שמעון, arriving at the palace.

phrases.english: Ben Temalyon, come out!
Ben Temalyon, come out!
And once they called him, he came out and left.
He said to them:
phrases.notes: Now the emperor is talking, thanking them for healing his daughter.

phrases.aramaic: שְׁאִילוּ כׇּל מָה דְּאִית לְכוֹן לְמִישְׁאַל.
phrases.english: Ask for anything you want to ask.
And he brought them into his treasury
to take whatever they wanted.
They found that letter,
phrases.notes: This is the letter with the decrees against the Jews that they came to cancel.

phrases.english: they took it and tore it up.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows the miracle that רבי שמעון accepted in the previous step actually happening.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The demon's help led to the decree being torn up and canceled.

steps.title: Linking the story to the פרוכת seen in Rome
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא connects this visit to the treasury with רבי אלעזר בר רבי יוסי's statement that he saw the פרוכת in Rome with drops of blood on it.
steps.simpleTranslation: And this is what רבי אלעזר בר רבי יוסי meant when he said: I saw it in the city of Rome, and there were several drops of blood on it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds a side note. A known statement of רבי אלעזר בר רבי יוסי makes sense because of this story.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אלעזר is the same son who traveled with רבי שמעון. When the emperor let them into his treasury, he saw items taken from the בית המקדש, including the פרוכת. So the story explains when and how he saw it.

keyTerms.meaning: And this is (what was meant); links a known statement to this story

steps.whyThisMatters: It ties the story to the history of the בית המקדש's holy objects that were taken to Rome.

phrases.aramaic: וְהַיְינוּ דְּאָמַר רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בַּר רַבִּי יוֹסֵי:
phrases.english: And this is what Rabbi Elazar bar Rabbi Yosei said:
I saw it in the city of Rome,
phrases.notes: "It" is the פרוכת, the curtain from the בית המקדש.

phrases.english: and there were several drops of blood on it.
phrases.notes: This is blood sprinkled toward the פרוכת on יום כיפור.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהַיְינוּ דְּאָמַר רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בַּר רַבִּי יוֹסֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the treasury visit from step 9 as the background for a known statement.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי אלעזר saw the פרוכת during the visit to the emperor's treasury.

steps.title: New משנה: פיגול and נותר do not combine
steps.stepSummary: A new משנה rules that פיגול and נותר do not join together to make up the minimum amount, because they are two separate prohibitions.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: פיגול and נותר do not combine, because they are two different names.
steps.whatsHappening: The story is over, and a new משנה begins. It returns to halacha, about mixing small amounts of different forbidden קדשים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Many rules need a minimum amount, like a כזית. The משנה says half a כזית of פיגול plus half a כזית of נותר do not add up, because each one has its own name. Step 13 limits this to the rabbinic טומאת ידים; for the איסור of eating, they do join.

keyTerms.meaning: A קרבן made invalid by a wrong intention about when it would be eaten
קרבן meat left over past its allowed time
Join together to reach the minimum amount
Two names: two separate categories of איסור

steps.confusionAlert: Don't conclude that פיגול and נותר never add up. The גמרא in Step 13 limits this משנה to טומאת ידים. For the איסור of eating, they do join, because one shared לאו covers all disqualified קדשים (Step 14).

phrases.english: MISHNA
Piggul and notar
do not join together,
phrases.notes: Together they don't add up to a כזית. The גמרא soon says this is only for טומאת ידים, not for eating.

phrases.english: because they are two names.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a brand-new topic after the story ends.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: פיגול and נותר do not combine, because they are two names. The גמרא limits this to טומאת ידים.

steps.title: Different sources of טומאה do not combine
steps.stepSummary: The משנה goes on: שרץ with נבלה, and נבלה with בשר המת, do not join together to make something טמא, not even for the easier of the two amounts.
steps.simpleTranslation: A שרץ and a נבלה, and likewise a נבלה and the flesh of a dead person, do not join with each other to make something impure, not even for the more lenient of the two.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה uses the same idea for טומאה: different kinds of impure things cannot be added together to reach the needed size.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each source of טומאה has its own minimum size. You might think the bigger amount (the more lenient one) could at least be reached by adding both. The משנה says no: they never combine, even for that.

keyTerms.meaning: A dead creeping creature that makes things טמא
An animal that died without proper שחיטה
The more lenient of the two (the one that needs the larger amount)

steps.whatToRemember: Different categories, whether איסורים or types of טומאה, do not add together to reach a minimum amount.

phrases.english: The creeping creature and the animal carcass,
and likewise the animal carcass and the flesh of a corpse

phrases.aramaic: אֵין מִצְטָרְפִין זֶה עִם זֶה לְטַמֵּא,
phrases.english: do not join with each other to make something impure,
not even for the more lenient of the two.
phrases.notes: "More lenient" means the one that needs the bigger amount to make something טמא.

steps.triggerLanguage: הַשֶּׁרֶץ וְהַנְּבֵלָה וְכֵן הַנְּבֵלָה וּבְשַׂר הַמֵּת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the 'no combining' idea from פיגול and נותר for sources of טומאה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: שרץ, נבלה and בשר המת do not combine to make something טמא, even for the larger, more lenient amount.

steps.title: שמואל limits the משנה to טומאת ידים
steps.stepSummary: שמואל says that פיגול and נותר do not join only for the rabbinic טומאת ידים. For the prohibition of eating, they do join.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said in the name of שמואל: The משנה only taught this for טומאת ידים, which is a rabbinic law. But for eating, they do join together.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא narrows the משנה from Step 11. The rule that פיגול and נותר do not join is said only about making the hands טמא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה said פיגול and נותר do not join. שמואל explains that this is only about טומאת ידים, a rule made by the רבנן, so it can be treated more lightly. When it comes to the איסור of eating, the two pieces do add up to the minimum amount.

keyTerms.meaning: They only taught this for... (limits a משנה to a narrower case)
Impurity of the hands, a rabbinic form of טומאה
From the רבנן, a rabbinic law rather than a Torah law

phrases.aramaic: גְּמָ׳ אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל:
phrases.english: GEMARA: Rav Yehuda said that Shmuel said:
They only taught this for impurity of the hands,
phrases.notes: He means the rule from the משנה that פיגול and נותר do not join together.

phrases.english: which is from the Rabbis.
But regarding eating, they join together.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Limits the scope of the משנה in Step 11
steps.mimraCoreRuling: פיגול and נותר do not join for rabbinic טומאת ידים, but they do join for the איסור of eating.

steps.title: Proof from רבי אליעזר: one prohibition covers all disqualified קדשים
steps.stepSummary: רבי אליעזר learns from a פסוק that anything holy that became פסול falls under one לא תעשה for eating. So פיגול and נותר share one איסור and can join.
steps.simpleTranslation: As a ברייתא teaches: רבי אליעזר says, 'It shall not be eaten because it is holy' teaches that anything holy that became disqualified gets a לא תעשה for eating it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא to support שמואל's claim that for eating, פיגול and נותר join together.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק gives one general לא תעשה against eating any disqualified קדשים. Since פיגול and נותר both fall under this one shared איסור, eating some of each adds up to the minimum amount. This explains why eating is different from טומאת ידים.

keyTerms.meaning: A negative commandment, a Torah prohibition

steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that two items with different names can still join if one shared איסור covers both of them.

phrases.english: As it is taught: Rabbi Eliezer says:
"It shall not be eaten because it is holy"
phrases.notes: שמות 29:34

phrases.english: anything holy that is disqualified,
the verse comes to give a prohibition
on eating it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the second half of שמואל's statement
steps.raayaObject: שמואל's ruling that פיגול and נותר join for eating
steps.raayaSupportSource: ברייתא of רבי אליעזר on the פסוק 'לא יאכל כי קדש הוא'

steps.title: Foods with different levels of טומאה join for the lighter level
steps.stepSummary: Food made טמא by an אב הטומאה and food made טמא by a ולד הטומאה join to reach the minimum amount. Together they pass on only the lighter level of טומאה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Food that became טמא from an אב הטומאה and food that became טמא from a ולד הטומאה join together to make things טמא at the lighter of the two levels.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It teaches that two foods with different levels of טומאה can be put together to reach the minimum size.
steps.deeperAnalysis: One food is a ראשון (first level), and the other is a שני (second level). Each alone may be too small, but together they reach the needed size. The combined food then makes things טמא only at the weaker level.

keyTerms.meaning: A main source of טומאה, which makes things a ראשון
Something that became טמא from another source, which makes things a שני

steps.confusionAlert: This is not like Step 12, where שרץ and נבלה did not join. There the two were different kinds of טומאה. Here it is the same kind of food טומאה, just at different levels.

phrases.english: MISHNA: Food that became impure from a primary source of impurity,
and food that became impure from a secondary source of impurity,
join together with each other
to make impure at the lighter of the two.
phrases.notes: The minimum amount here is the size of an egg, and the lighter level is the second level.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: New משנה, continuing the theme of joining amounts
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A ראשון and a שני join to reach the minimum amount, and they make things טמא at the level of a שני.

steps.title: All foods join for the standard food amounts
steps.stepSummary: All foods join for פסול הגויה with חצי פרס, two meals for עירוב, a כביצה for food טומאה, a גרוגרת for carrying on שבת, and a כותבת on יום הכפורים.
steps.simpleTranslation: All foods join together to disqualify the body with half a פרס, for two meals for an עירוב, for an egg's size to make food טמא, for a dried fig's size for carrying out on שבת, and for a date's size on יום הכפורים.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה lists many halachos with a minimum amount of food. In all of them, different kinds of food add up together.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In each case, what matters is how much food there is, not which kind of food. So different foods can be combined to reach the חצי פרס, the two meals, the כביצה, the גרוגרת, or the כותבת.

keyTerms.meaning: Disqualifying the body, so that a person who ate טמא food may not eat תרומה
Half of a half-loaf, the amount for פסול הגויה
Food placed to extend the שבת boundary
A dried fig, the amount for carrying out on שבת
A large date, the amount for eating on יום הכפורים

phrases.aramaic: כׇּל הָאוֹכָלִים מִצְטָרְפִין זֶה עִם זֶה
phrases.english: All the foods join together with each other
to disqualify the body, at half a peras.
And as for food for two meals, for an eruv,
phrases.notes: This means the joining of שבת boundaries.

phrases.english: and an egg's size, to make impure with food impurity,
and a dried fig's size, for carrying out on Shabbat,
and a large date's size, on Yom Kippur.

steps.triggerLanguage: כׇּל הָאוֹכָלִים מִצְטָרְפִין זֶה עִם זֶה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: The משנה continues with a list of food amounts
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In all these food amounts, different foods add up together.

steps.title: All liquids join for the standard drinking amounts
steps.stepSummary: All liquids join to make a רביעית for פסול הגויה and a מלא לוגמא on יום הכפורים.
steps.simpleTranslation: All liquids join together to disqualify the body with a רביעית, and to make a cheekful on יום הכפורים.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה finishes with the same idea for drinks: different liquids add up together.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Just as with foods, the type of drink does not matter. Different liquids combine to reach the רביעית that disqualifies the body, or the cheekful that makes a person liable on יום הכפורים.

keyTerms.meaning: A quarter of a לוג, the amount for פסול הגויה with liquids
A cheekful, the amount for drinking on יום הכפורים

steps.whatToRemember: For these minimum amounts, all foods join with each other and all liquids join with each other.

phrases.aramaic: כׇּל הַמַּשְׁקִין מִצְטָרְפִין זוֹ עִם זוֹ
phrases.english: All the liquids join together with each other
to disqualify the body, at a quarter-log,
and a cheekful, on Yom Kippur.

steps.triggerLanguage: כׇּל הַמַּשְׁקִין מִצְטָרְפִין זוֹ עִם זוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Same rule as Step 16, now applied to liquids
steps.mimraCoreRuling: All liquids join for רביעית and for מלא לוגמא.

steps.title: רבי שמעון explains why a ראשון and a שני join
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון gives a reason for the משנה in Step 15: a שני can become, or produce, a ראשון.
steps.simpleTranslation: A ברייתא teaches: רבי שמעון says, what is the reason? Because it is possible for the second level to become first level.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings רבי שמעון's reason for why food at two different levels of טומאה can join together.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally we might expect two different levels to stay separate. רבי שמעון says they are close enough to join, because a שני can lead to a ראשון. This sets up the challenge in the next step.

phrases.english: GEMARA: It is taught: Rabbi Shimon says:
What is the reason?
phrases.notes: He is asking why the ראשון and the שני from the משנה join together.

phrases.english: Because it is possible for the second-level to be made first-level.

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּנְיָא, רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן אוֹמֵר: מָה טַעַם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a reason for the first rule of the משנה
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A ראשון and a שני join because a שני can lead to a ראשון.

steps.title: Challenge: a שני cannot make a ראשון
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how a שני could ever produce a ראשון, since that is impossible.
steps.simpleTranslation: But does a שני make a ראשון? That is not possible!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks רבי שמעון's reason. A food at the second level can only pass on a lower level, never the first level.
steps.deeperAnalysis: טומאה goes down one level each time it passes on. A שני touching food makes it a שלישי, not a ראשון. So רבי שמעון's reason seems to rest on something that cannot happen.

phrases.english: But does a second-level make a first-level?
That is not possible!
phrases.notes: A שני that touches food makes it a third level, not a first level.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבי שמעון's reason
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי שמעון's reason that a שני can become a ראשון
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: טומאה only goes down in level, so a שני can never produce a ראשון.

steps.title: רבא: The שני was caused by the ראשון
steps.stepSummary: רבא explains that רבי שמעון did not mean a שני literally produces a ראשון. He meant that the ראשון is what caused the שני in the first place.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: This is what רבי שמעון means. What caused the food to become a שני? Wasn't it a ראשון?!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question from Step 19 by giving a new reading of רבי שמעון's words. רבא says we misunderstood what רבי שמעון meant.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question in Step 19 assumed רבי שמעון meant a שני can turn something into a ראשון, which is impossible. רבא flips the direction: the ראשון caused the שני. Since both come from the same chain, it makes sense that they can join together.

keyTerms.meaning: "This is what he means." Used when the גמרא re-reads someone's words to fix a difficulty.

steps.confusionAlert: רבא is not saying a שני can create a ראשון. He is saying the opposite: the ראשון created the שני, and that shared origin is the reason they join.

phrases.english: Rava said: This is what he is saying:
phrases.notes: "He" is רבי שמעון from Step 18.

phrases.english: What caused the second-level food?
Was it not a first-level food?!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא in Step 19 by re-reading רבי שמעון's statement.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Re-reading the statement: the direction of cause is reversed.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי שמעון seemed to say that a שני produces a ראשון, which is impossible.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי שמעון meant that the ראשון caused the שני, so both share one source and can join.

steps.title: רב אשי: ראשון and שני are one household when it comes to a שלישי
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי gives another explanation: when you look at what they do to a שלישי, the ראשון and the שני are like members of one house.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said: A ראשון and a שני, when it comes to a שלישי, are members of one household.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second answer to the question from Step 19. רב אשי explains the link between ראשון and שני in a different way than רבא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא looked back at where the שני came from. רב אשי looks forward: both a ראשון and a שני end up leading to a שלישי. Because they connect to the same next level, they count like one family and can join together.

keyTerms.meaning: With regard to, when it comes to
Members of one house, meaning they belong to the same group

steps.whatToRemember: Food with different levels of טומאה can join together because they are connected: רבא says the ראשון caused the שני, and רב אשי says both lead to the שלישי like one household.

phrases.english: Rav Ashi said:
A first-level and a second-level food, with regard to a third-level food,
are members of one house.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a second answer to the same קשיא that רבא answered in Step 20.
steps.terutzResolutionType: A different reason for the connection: shared effect on the next level instead of shared cause.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A ראשון and a שני seem to be different levels that should not join.
steps.terutzMaskana: Since both lead to a שלישי, they are like one household and join together.
